findings.reason: §6 should cite the landed carry and rescope the node to what is genuinely absent — the imas-ambix D4 qualification — since the codex-pause lift it waits on is itself already resolved (f-awcwyh-codex-pause-lifted); otherwise the node re-lands existing machinery.
findings.text: §6's first deliverable, "Node harness-home-carries-the-operator-config (r-20260925T165045662374) makes each backend declare in flight config the operator-home files its harness reads", is already shipped: reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml:40-48 declares exactly claude {settings.json filtered to hooks; CLAUDE.md} and codex {AGENTS.md; config.toml; rules}, reckon/flight.py:232-300 exposes harness_home_files / harness_home_adjacent_files / shipped_harness_home_files, and reckon/_backends.py:2129 seed_harness_home consumes the declaration on the production launch path; §2's own carry records (c-20260926T0735-harness-home-adjacent-carry and the c-20260926T1130 carry-opt-in comment) already report this landed, including the ~/.claude.json home-root carry at revision 14006c1e. The section states shipped behaviour as pending work.

findings.reason: §3 should name routing._workspace_roots as the owner and compose the protected worktree root from it (env override included), so the seal follows placement instead of forking it.
findings.text: the fence's shipped protected default names the worktree pool as the literal root / "Code" / ".reckon-worktrees", duplicating the placement owner reckon/crew/routing.py:487 _workspace_roots, which computes the pool as repo.parent / ".reckon-worktrees" and honours the RECKON_WORKTREE_ROOT override plus a legacy /tmp/reckon-worktrees fallback; a second component literal sits at reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:224. Because the fence does not read that owner, a worktree placed under an override root, or a repository that is not a child of ~/Code, is not sealed — the fence seals a path that may hold no worktrees while the real pool stays writable, contradicting §3's claim that "every other run's worktree is then read-only to a fenced worker".

findings.reason: one deep module (a write-scope value with roots(), contains(path), ensure()) would retire the three containment spellings and the second root list before the next node builds on them, and the plan's own rework record (commits 1de2d086 and af310d81) shows the split has already forced two corrections.
findings.text: the write-scope behaviour is spread across delivery_write_roots:85, sandbox_write_roots:123, fenced_write_roots:210 and fenced_write_roots's declared-path handling, while containment is computed three different ways: inline Path.is_relative_to in _declared_write_grant:190, _within_any(target, sealed) in fence_argv:3098, and an inline equality/relative test in _fenced_worktree_refusal:2850; resolved_destination:2859 is a bare rename of Path.resolve(). No single interface owns "which resolved paths may this run write".

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the fence's write-scope concept has no single home; its roots are computed by three functions and containment is tested three separate ways in reckon/_backends.py.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the fence's protected default hardcodes the worktree pool at reckon/_backends.py:2683 instead of composing it from the placement owner reckon/crew/routing.py:487 _workspace_roots.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6 proposes rebuilding the harness-home carry that already ships in reckon/flight-defaults.yaml, reckon/flight.py and seed_harness_home, and should cite it instead.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the fence helpers the plan adds each carry a docstring stating why the existing machinery cannot be extended (fenced_write_roots over sandbox_write_roots, the git shim over the shell could not be parsed), which is the justification this item asks for.
